# Lockers module for AccessBuddy: build spec

Worktree: `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/.worktrees/lockers`, branch `feat/lockers` (off `origin/main`, v1.23.4). Work ONLY in this worktree.

Source being replaced (read it, it is short): legacy Google Apps Script at
`/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/lifesaving/smlsc/club-renewal/artifacts/legacy-lockers/lockers/` (Allocations.js, Revoke.js, EmailService.js, the three `*Email.html` templates).
Legacy data: `/home/nicholas-wood/.claude/jobs/7506614f/tmp/lockers/lockers.xlsx` (REAL MEMBER PII: never commit it, never copy rows into tests, fixtures, commit messages or the PR).

Nick (product owner) confirmed the journey and these decisions on 2026-11-16. Do not re-litigate them.

## 1. Confirmed product decisions

1. Lockers is a per-tenant module switched by `settings.lockersEnabled`, which ONLY a global admin can change. Club admins cannot see or set it.
2. Two new permissions, separate from all existing ones:
   - `approve_lockers` ("Approve lockers"): approve (which allocates in the same step), decline, revoke, assign a locker directly to a member.
   - `update_lockers` ("Update lockers"): locker areas and inventory, move a member between lockers, mark label / clean-out tasks done; receives the clean-out notifications.
   Club admins and global admins hold both (existing behaviour of `checkPermission`).
3. Approve and allocate are ONE step. Revoke sits under `approve_lockers`.
4. Lockers are requested through the SAME public request form as fobs, so a person enters their details once. A locker can be requested alone, or added to a "new fob" request.
5. A QR code for the locker request exists the same way the Front Door QR does today.
6. A member's locker shows on the admin member page and on the member dashboard, in the same style credentials do.
7. No hard limit on lockers per member. The approver sees a warning if the member already holds one.
8. Season confirmation (attestation): a member holding a locker is asked whether they want to keep it. "No" releases the locker.
9. Renewal cutoff: a club-admin setting (month + day; SMLSC will use 1 December). After that date each season, lockers held by members who have not renewed for the current season are released and sent to the `update_lockers` holders to clean out and clear the label.
10. Emails MUST be sent for allocation, decline and revoke (legacy behaviour), with the tenant's locker policy attached when one is uploaded. This must be proven by tests.
11. No fees. Areas are generic and tenant-defined ("Male Changeroom", "Female Changeroom" are SMLSC data, never hard-coded).
12. Import SMLSC's spreadsheet with a dry-run-first importer. Do NOT run it against production; local dry-run only.

## 2. Data model (migration `0021_lockers.sql`, hand-written, plus journal entry and Drizzle schema `packages/db/src/schema/lockers.ts` exported from `schema/index.ts`)

All four tables: `tenant_id uuid not null references tenants`, RLS ENABLE + FORCE, the two policies used in `0013_email_queue.sql` (isolation + insert check), and the table names added to `RLS_TABLES` in `packages/db/src/rls.ts`. Statuses are text columns (repo convention), values enumerated in `packages/shared/src/enums.ts`.

- `locker_areas`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `name`, `sort_order int default 0`, `active bool default true`, timestamps. Unique `(tenant_id, name)`.
- `lockers`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `area_id` fk, `number int`, `level text null` (free text, e.g. Top/Middle/Bottom), `status text default 'available'` (`available | single_use | out_of_service`), `label_update_required bool default false`, `cleanout_required bool default false`, `notes text null`, timestamps. Unique `(area_id, number)`. Only `available` lockers can be allocated. `single_use` = day-use locker, never allocated (legacy "SINGLE USE" rows).
- `locker_requests`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `user_id uuid null` fk users, `area_id` fk, `requested_number int null`, `status text default 'pending'` (`pending | allocated | declined | cancelled`), `policy_accepted_at timestamptz null`, requester snapshot `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone` (always stored, lower-cased email), `related_fob_request_id uuid null` fk fob_requests, `decided_by uuid null`, `decided_at`, `decline_reason text null`, `allocation_id uuid null`, timestamps. Index `(tenant_id, status)`.
- `locker_allocations`: `id`, `tenant_id`, `locker_id` fk, `user_id uuid null` fk users, holder snapshot `holder_email`, `holder_first_name`, `holder_last_name`, `holder_phone`, `request_id uuid null`, `allocated_at`, `allocated_by uuid null`, `kept_for_season text null`, `ended_at timestamptz null`, `ended_by uuid null`, `end_type text null` (`revoked | released | not_renewed | moved`), `end_reason text null`, timestamps. PARTIAL UNIQUE index on `(locker_id) where ended_at is null` (one active holder per locker). Index `(tenant_id, user_id)`.
  `user_id` is nullable only so imported legacy holders whose email matches no member can be carried; every allocation created through the app has a `user_id`.
- `attestation_requests`: add `locker_responses jsonb null` (`{ allocationId: string; keep: boolean }[]`).

Add `AuditEntityType` values `locker` and `locker_request`.

## 3. Settings

In `tenantSettingsSchema` (`packages/shared/src/schemas.ts`), all optional on read (stored JSON is never parsed through the schema; every reader must treat `undefined` as off / unset):
- `lockersEnabled: boolean` (default false).
- `lockerCutoffMonth: 1..12`, `lockerCutoffDay: 1..31` (both unset = cutoff rule off).
- `lockerPolicy: { name: string; path: string; uploadedAt: string } | undefined` (set only by the upload route).

Guarding `lockersEnabled` (CRITICAL): `PUT /api/v1/t/[slug]/config/settings` ends in `.passthrough()` and shallow-merges, and the settings page posts the whole settings object back. That route must ALWAYS preserve the stored `lockersEnabled` and `lockerPolicy` regardless of the body (strip both keys from the incoming body before merging), for every caller including global admins. The flag is changed only by a new `PATCH /api/v1/platform/tenants/[id]` (`isGlobalAdmin` or 403; body `{ lockersEnabled: boolean }`; merges into settings; audit entry `action: "tenant_feature_update"` with before/after). UI: a "Lockers" switch/checkbox per tenant on `app/admin/tenants/page.tsx` (the platform page; leave the orphan `t/[slug]/admin/tenants` page alone). The platform GET must return each tenant's `lockersEnabled`.

Club-admin settings page (`admin/config/settings/page.tsx`), shown only when `lockersEnabled`: a "Lockers" card with cutoff month + day number inputs (validate real dates, e.g. reject 31 for a 30-day month; allow clearing both), the policy PDF upload (new route `config/locker-policy`: POST multipart `policy`, PDF only by magic bytes `%PDF`, 5 MB max, `CONFIGURE`; DELETE to remove; storage mirrors `config/logo/route.ts`: GCS `tenants/${slug}-locker-policy.pdf` in `GCS_ASSETS_BUCKET`, `public/tenants/` fallback in dev, refuse on Cloud Run without a bucket; public GET streams the PDF so the request form can link it), and a second QR code (reuse the existing `QRCode` component) encoding `${origin}/t/${slug}/request?type=locker`, captioned for lockers.

Extract the season-label rule into one pure helper (e.g. `seasonForDate(date, tz)` in `apps/web/src/lib/timezone.ts`: on or after 1 July of year Y it is `"Y/Y+1"`, else `"Y-1/Y"`), consistent with `membershipYearExpiry`. Unit test it.

## 4. Lifecycle (every transition; implement in ONE service module `apps/web/src/lib/services/lockers.ts`, called by thin routes)

Request states: `pending -> allocated | declined | cancelled`. No other transitions. A request that is not `pending` cannot be approved, declined or cancelled (409).

- SUBMIT (public): creates `locker_requests` pending. Refuse (409, friendly message) a second pending request from the same email for the same tenant. Resolve `user_id` by lower-cased email at submit time when a user with a membership in this tenant exists. Emails: `lockerRequestReceived` to the requester; admin notification `lockerRequestNeedsApproval` to holders of `approve_lockers` via `sendAdminNotification`. Audit on the request.
- APPROVE (`approve_lockers`, body `{ lockerId }`): re-resolve the requester by email if `user_id` is null. If they are still not a user with a membership in this tenant, refuse 409 "This person is not a member yet. Approve their access request first." Locker must be in the request's tenant, `available`, with no active allocation (also rely on the partial unique index; translate the violation to 409 "That locker has just been allocated"). In one transaction: insert allocation, set request `allocated` + `allocation_id` + decided fields, set `lockers.label_update_required = true`, audit on request AND locker. After commit: email `lockerAllocated` (number, area, level) with the policy PDF attached if uploaded. The approver may pick ANY available locker in ANY area (the requested area/number is a preference).
- DECLINE (`approve_lockers`, body `{ reason }` required, 1..500 chars): request `declined`, email `lockerDeclined` with the reason (policy attached if uploaded), audit.
- CANCEL: the requester (signed in, own request) or an `approve_lockers` holder cancels a pending request. No email.
- ASSIGN DIRECT (`approve_lockers`, body `{ lockerId, userId }`): allocation with no request, for a member of this tenant. Same checks, same email + label flag as approve.
- REVOKE (`approve_lockers`, body `{ reason }` required): ends the active allocation (`end_type: revoked`), sets the locker `label_update_required` and `cleanout_required` true, emails the holder `lockerRevoked` (reason, 7 days to remove belongings; policy attached if uploaded), notifies `update_lockers` holders (`lockerCleanoutRequired`, one locker), audit on locker (and member where the audit trail is keyed by user).
- MOVE (`update_lockers`, body `{ lockerId }`): ends the allocation (`moved`, no clean-out flag on the old locker but `label_update_required` true on BOTH lockers) and creates a new one for the same holder in the target locker, one transaction; emails the holder `lockerAllocated` for the new locker with wording that it replaces the old one.
- TASKS (`update_lockers`): mark `label_update_required` false and/or `cleanout_required` false on a locker. Audit.
- INVENTORY (`update_lockers`): areas CRUD; lockers create single, bulk-create a number range in an area (skip numbers that exist, report them), edit level/notes/status, delete only when the locker has no allocation rows at all (otherwise refuse and suggest `out_of_service`). A locker with an active allocation cannot be set to `single_use` or `out_of_service` (409).
- KEEP / RELEASE via season confirmation (section 7).
- CUTOFF release (section 8).
- LINK: helper `linkLockerHoldersByEmail(tx, tenantId)` sets `user_id` on allocations and pending requests where it is null and the snapshot email matches a user with a membership in the tenant. Called at approve, by the daily cron per tenant, and by the importer.

Suggested locker (pure function, unit tested, shown pre-selected to the approver): the requested number in the requested area if it is free; otherwise the middle of the longest run of consecutive free `available` lockers in that area (numbers ordered ascending; `single_use`, `out_of_service` and occupied lockers break runs); `null` when the area has none free. This is the legacy rule with its bugs removed (legacy scanned only 1..41 and compared names loosely; do not reproduce those).

Members without a locker: nothing changes for them anywhere.

Module gate: EVERY lockers API route (public and admin) returns 404 when `lockersEnabled` is not true for the tenant. Every UI entry point is hidden when it is off.

## 5. API routes (under `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/lockers/`; follow existing helpers `withTenantAuth`, `checkPermission`/`checkAnyPermission`, `withTenant`, `resolveTenant`)

- `GET lockers` (either locker permission): areas with lockers, active holder (name, email, phone, since, kept_for_season, linked user id), task flags.
- `GET lockers/requests?status=` (either permission), each pending row carries `suggestedLockerId`, the requester's membership state (member / not yet a member), and how many active lockers they already hold.
- `POST lockers/requests/submit` (public, per-IP rate limit like the fob submit route): locker-only request.
- `POST lockers/requests/[id]/approve | decline | cancel`.
- `POST lockers/allocations` (assign direct), `POST lockers/allocations/[id]/revoke`, `POST lockers/allocations/[id]/move`.
- `POST|PUT|DELETE lockers/areas[/id]`, `POST lockers/items` (single or `{ areaId, from, to, levels?: string[] }` bulk: levels cycle in order, e.g. Top, Middle, Bottom), `PUT|DELETE lockers/items/[id]`, `POST lockers/items/[id]/tasks`.
- `GET lockers/cutoff-preview` (either permission): the allocations the cutoff rule would release if it ran today, and holders it cannot evaluate (unlinked).
- Fob submit route `requests/submit/route.ts`: optional body field `locker: { areaId: uuid, requestedNumber?: int, policyAccepted: true }`, accepted ONLY when `requestType === "new"` and the module is on. The locker request is created in the same transaction with `related_fob_request_id`. If the module is off, ignore the field silently is NOT acceptable: reject 400.

zod schemas for all bodies live in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts`. The admins API currently accepts any string as a permission; leave that as is.

## 6. UI

Journey to preserve exactly:
1. Global admin ticks "Lockers" for the club on the platform Tenants page.
2. Member opens the request form (button on the club landing page `t/[slug]/page.tsx` "Request a locker", or the locker QR, both -> `/t/{slug}/request?type=locker`). The request page reads `?type=locker` and preselects the new "Locker" type card (only offered when the module is on and at least one active area has lockers). Steps for type `locker`: Type -> Details (first name, last name, email, phone; prefilled and read-only identity when signed in) -> Locker (area select using the base-ui Select explicit-children pattern, optional preferred number, policy checkbox "I agree to follow the locker policy" with a link to the policy PDF when uploaded; checkbox is required) -> Review -> success screen "Locker request submitted".
   For type `new` (new fob): an extra optional "Locker" step before Review: "Would you also like to request a locker?" Off by default; when ticked it shows the same area / preferred number / policy controls and the Review step lists it. One submit creates both.
3. Admin nav gets a "Lockers" item (shown when module on AND the admin holds either locker permission). Page `t/[slug]/admin/lockers/page.tsx` with three parts:
   - Requests: pending requests, each with the suggested locker preselected in a locker picker (area + number, any available locker), badges "Already holds locker X" / "Not a member yet", buttons Approve and Decline (decline asks for a reason). Shown/enabled only with `approve_lockers`.
   - Lockers: per-area grid/list of every locker: number, level, status, holder, since; actions Revoke (`approve_lockers`, asks reason), Move (`update_lockers`), Assign (`approve_lockers`, member picker), and inventory controls (`update_lockers`): add area, bulk-add lockers, edit status/level/notes.
   - To do: lockers with `label_update_required` or `cleanout_required`, each with "Label done" / "Cleaned out" buttons (`update_lockers`). When a cutoff is configured, a "At the cutoff (D Month)" panel listing what `cutoff-preview` returns.
4. Admin member page: a "Lockers" card between `CredentialActions` and `AttestationSection`, only when the module is on: active lockers (area, number, level, since, kept-for-season), pending request, history (ended allocations with end type + reason), Revoke / Assign (`approve_lockers`) and Move (`update_lockers`). Locker and locker-request ids join the page's audit trail. Members list: a small "Locker" chip next to the fob breakdown for members holding one.
5. Member dashboard: a "My Locker" section (module on only): active locker(s), a pending request with a Cancel button, otherwise a "Request a locker" link.
6. Admins page: `PERMISSION_LABELS` gets "Approve lockers" and "Update lockers". The two locker checkboxes are listed only when the tenant has the module on (the page needs the flag from the API).
7. Audit: labels for every new `metadata.action` in BOTH renderers (`components/audit-trail.tsx` and `admin/audit/page.tsx`), entity type labels + filter options + the `entityLabel` SQL CASE for `locker` ("Area N") and `locker_request`.

Copy rules: Australian English, plain language, no em dashes, first-name-only email greetings. Follow the existing shadcn-on-base-ui components; base-ui `SelectValue` needs explicit children.

## 7. Season confirmation

- `GET attestations/[token]`: for a whole-membership renewal (`credentialIds` null) when the module is on, also return `lockers: [{ allocationId, areaName, number, level }]` for the member's active allocations. Never for scoped confirmations.
- Attest page: under the fobs, a "Your locker" block per locker with a checkbox, checked by default, "I want to keep locker {area} {number} for {season}". Unchecked shows "This locker will be released. Please remove your belongings and lock within 7 days." The Confirm button must render when the member has fobs OR lockers (today it renders only with fobs).
- `POST`: body gains optional `lockerResponses: [{ allocationId, keep }]`. Reject allocation ids that are not this member's active allocations in this tenant. Persist to `attestation_requests.locker_responses`. `keep: true` sets `kept_for_season = season`. `keep: false` ends the allocation (`released`, reason "Member chose not to keep the locker for {season}"), flags label + clean-out, emails the member `lockerRevoked` with that reason, notifies `update_lockers` holders, audits. A locker the member holds but that is missing from the body is treated as keep (old clients).
- Admin `AttestationSection` history line mentions locker answers ("locker kept" / "locker released").
- `force-renew` and `confirm-on-behalf` do not touch lockers.

## 8. Cutoff rule (daily cron, new step after 1b2, per tenant, inside `withTenant`)

For each tenant with `lockersEnabled` and both cutoff fields set: compute the current season with `seasonForDate(now, tz)` and the cutoff instant = tenant-local midnight of the first occurrence of (month, day) on or after 1 July of the season's start year (1 December -> December of the start year; 1 February -> February of the end year). If `now >= cutoff`: every ACTIVE allocation with a linked `user_id` whose membership in this tenant is missing, not `active`, or has `current_season !== currentSeason` is ended (`not_renewed`, reason "Membership not renewed for {season} by {cutoff date}"), its locker flagged label + clean-out, and the member emailed `lockerRevoked` with that reason. ONE `lockerCleanoutRequired` notification per tenant per run lists every locker released in that run and goes to `update_lockers` holders. Idempotent: a second run the same day releases nothing and sends nothing. Unlinked allocations are never auto-released. The step also calls `linkLockerHoldersByEmail` first. A failure in one tenant must not stop the others (match the existing try/catch style of step 1b).

## 9. Emails

New templates in `lib/email-templates.ts` + wiring in `lib/services/email.ts` (`TemplateVariables`, `renderTemplate` cases) + registry entries in `packages/shared/src/email-events.ts`: `lockerRequestReceived`, `lockerAllocated`, `lockerDeclined`, `lockerRevoked` (member), `lockerRequestNeedsApproval`, `lockerCleanoutRequired` (admin). Content follows the three legacy templates (read them) but tenant-branded via the existing layout, never mentioning SMLSC by name, and using the tenant's reply/support address the way other templates do.
- Member emails with a policy attachment are sent directly with `sendTemplatedEmail(..., attachments, audit)` (the queue cannot carry attachments). Read the PDF bytes straight from storage (GCS or the dev fallback); do NOT go through `fetchAttachments` (it needs an absolute public URL). A missing or unreadable policy must not block the email: send without it and log.
- Respect `sendEmails` exactly as other templates do; every send carries the audit context so the audit entry has `subject`.
- Send after the DB transaction commits (or follow the pattern the revoke-credential route uses) so a rolled-back approve never emails.

## 10. Importer `packages/db/src/import-lockers.ts`

Modelled on `migrate-smlsc.ts`: `--file <xlsx> --tenant <slug>`, `--dry-run` default, `--commit` to write, JSON report to `packages/db/migrations-out/` (gitignored), idempotent (re-running changes nothing). Sheets: "Male Changeroom Allocations" / "Female Changeroom Allocations" (columns Locker Number, Level, First Name, Last Name, Date Allocated, Notes, Contact Number, Email Address, Request Number, ...) and "Locker Requests".
- Areas: one per allocation sheet, named by stripping " Allocations" ("Male Changeroom", "Female Changeroom"). The requests sheet says "Male Changerooms"/"Female Changerooms": map by prefix.
- Lockers: one per numbered row; `SINGLE` / `USE` in the name columns -> `single_use`; level from the Level column.
- Allocations: a row with a first name that is not SINGLE USE -> active allocation; `allocated_at` from the Excel serial date (convert correctly, tenant timezone); phone numbers arrive as numbers that lost their leading zero (`4.38854431E8`) -> restore to `04xxxxxxxx`; match `user_id` by lower-cased email against users with a membership in the tenant, else leave null and list in the report as unmatched.
- `label_update_required`: true where the matching "Locker Requests" row has "Sticker Update Required" = 1.
- Pending requests: "Locker Requests" rows with no Approved value and no Revoked value and an email -> `pending` (preserve the timestamp as `created_at`, requested number, area).
- Never sends email. Report counts: areas, lockers, single-use, allocations (matched / unmatched), pending requests, label flags, skipped rows with reasons.
- Does not set `lockersEnabled` or the cutoff.

## 11. Tests (vitest; DB-gated suites use `describe.skipIf(!process.env.DATABASE_URL)` like `force-renew.test.ts`)

Run with `DATABASE_URL=postgres://accessbuddy:testpassword@127.0.0.1:54329/accessbuddy_lockers` (embedded Postgres already running; database already migrated to 0020; run `bun run db:migrate` after adding 0021). Baseline before this work: db 16, shared 27, web 378 passing, 0 skipped. All must stay green, with 0 skipped.

Must cover at minimum: suggested-locker function (requested free; requested taken; runs broken by single-use/occupied; none free); `seasonForDate` and the cutoff-instant computation (1 Dec and 1 Feb cases, boundary at local midnight); request state rules (approve twice -> 409; decline non-pending -> 409); approve refuses a non-member; the unique-index race path; revoke flags both tasks; move; the module gate (404 when off) on at least the public submit and one admin route; permission matrix (`approve_lockers` cannot do inventory/move/tasks; `update_lockers` cannot approve/decline/revoke/assign; neither -> 403); settings PUT cannot change `lockersEnabled` or `lockerPolicy`; platform PATCH refuses non-global-admins; combined fob+locker submit creates both rows and rejects `locker` on non-`new` types; attestation GET/POST locker keep and release (and rejection of a foreign allocation id); cutoff step releases only unrenewed linked holders after the cutoff, nothing before it, and is idempotent; EMAIL PROOF: allocation, decline and revoke each invoke the send path with the right template, recipient and (when a policy exists) an attachment, by spying/mocking at the same seam existing email tests use; importer parsing unit tests on SYNTHETIC rows (phone restore, Excel date, single-use detection). The `tenant-isolation` guard test must pass with the four new tables.

## 12. Gates and delivery

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run db:check-drift` (if it runs locally against the test database), `bun run test`: all exit 0 on the FINAL tree, run with turbo `--force` so nothing is served from cache, 0 skipped.
- Conventional commits, `feat(lockers): ...`. Commit in logical steps. Do NOT push, do NOT open a PR, do NOT touch `main`, do NOT run anything against production or over `ssh mac`.
- No new runtime dependencies without saying so in your report (`xlsx` is already a devDependency of `@accessbuddy/db`).
- Do not refactor unrelated code. Known unrelated defects to leave alone: the cross-tenant join in `buildAuthContext` (being fixed on a separate branch), unused `email_configurations` overrides, `PERMISSION_LABELS` gaps for existing permissions.

## 13. AMENDMENTS after design review (these OVERRIDE anything above that conflicts)

A. Concurrency. Every transition starts with a guarded write and stops on zero rows before doing anything else: requests `UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2 AND status = 'pending' RETURNING`; allocations `UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2 AND ended_at IS NULL RETURNING`. Zero rows -> 409, no insert, no email. Approve, assign, move and locker status edits take `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the locker row first. Add a partial unique index on `locker_requests (tenant_id, lower(email)) WHERE status = 'pending'` and translate its violation to the friendly 409. THE DEFECT (already confirmed by reading the code): `buildAuthContext` in `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts` (~L285-320) builds each membership's role with
```ts
.from(tenantMemberships)
.leftJoin(adminAssignments, eq(tenantMemberships.userId, adminAssignments.userId))
.where(eq(tenantMemberships.userId, dbUser.id));
```
The join is on user only, not tenant. `admin_assignments` rows are per tenant (`tenant_id` set, role_type `permissions` or `club_admin`) or global (`tenant_id` NULL, role_type `global_admin`). So a user who is an admin in tenant A and an ordinary member of tenant B gets A's role and permissions attached to their B membership, and `checkPermission` (`apps/web/src/lib/permissions.ts`) then grants them in B. It also multiplies rows when a user has more than one assignment. Harmless with one tenant today, a real cross-tenant privilege escalation once a second tenant exists.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
- A tenant-scoped assignment attaches only to the membership of the SAME tenant.
- A global-admin assignment (`tenant_id` NULL) must keep working exactly as today everywhere `isGlobalAdmin(auth)` and `checkPermission` are used. input.message:
REQUIRED BACKEND FIXES from an independent review of phase 1. Do these as their own commit(s) (`fix(lockers): ...`), each with a test that fails before the fix. Finish the UI file you are in the middle of first if you are mid-edit, then do these BEFORE continuing the rest of phase 2 (two of them change what the UI must show). Same rules as before; final gates at the end cover everything.

1. HIGH, cutoff "renewed" test (`lib/locker-cutoff.ts`, `holderReleasedByCutoff`): a holder whose `current_season` is a LATER season than the cutoff season is currently released (`"2027/2028" !== "2026/2027"`), so a June pre-season renewal drive would release every renewed holder. Fix: parse the start year of both seasons and treat the holder as renewed when membership start year >= cutoff season start year. An unparseable season string is "cannot evaluate" (see 2), never a release. Unit cases: same season kept; later season kept; earlier season released; garbage string not released.

2. HIGH, null `current_season` (this corrects spec section 8, which was wrong): memberships auto-created at fob approval, and some migrated operational users, have `current_season = NULL`. They must NEVER be auto-released. A holder with a null or unparseable season is "cannot evaluate": excluded from the release, and listed in `cutoff-preview` `cannotEvaluate` with `reason: "no_season_recorded"` (alongside the existing `"unlinked"`). Missing membership row or membership status not `active` still releases, as specified. Update the existing pure test that asserts null releases. Add a service test: new joiner (membership created this season, null season) holding a locker is not released by the cutoff run and appears in the preview's cannot-evaluate list. The cron's clean-out notification should also carry a short "could not be checked, please review" list of those lockers when the run is active and that list is non-empty, but only on a run that released at least one locker OR on the first active run of the season (do not send it every night: derive "first active run" from data you already have, e.g. no `locker_not_renewed` audit and no such notice yet this season; if that cannot be done cleanly, include the list only on runs that released something and say so in the report).

3. MEDIUM, arming vs module flag: (a) the settings PUT must refuse cutoff writes while `lockersEnabled` is not true (400 with a clear message); (b) `PATCH /api/v1/platform/tenants/[id]` must set `lockerCutoffArmedAt = now` whenever `lockersEnabled` goes from false/unset to true and a cutoff month/day is stored, so enabling the module after this season's date cannot act until next season. Tests: cutoff saved, module off then on after the date -> the run releases nothing and the preview says it first applies next season.

4. MEDIUM, combined fob + locker submit (`requests/submit/route.ts`): the Stripe PaymentIntent is created inside the transaction before the locker request insert, so a bad/inactive/foreign `areaId` or a racing duplicate rolls back after the intent already exists. Fix: validate the area (tenant filter, active, has at least one available locker, same rule as `public-config`) in the pre-check block BEFORE the transaction and 400 there; and inside the transaction insert the locker request BEFORE any payment call so a unique violation aborts before Stripe is touched. Test with payment required: bad area -> 400 and the payment-intent creator was not called.

5. MEDIUM, cutoff vs concurrent keep/renew (`services/locker-season.ts`): the release UPDATE must re-check at write time, not only in memory: add `kept_for_season IS DISTINCT FROM <season>` to the guarded UPDATE, and re-evaluate the membership inside the same statement (a `NOT EXISTS` on a membership row that counts as renewed under rule 1, or select the candidates `FOR UPDATE OF locker_allocations` and re-read the membership inside the transaction before ending). Test: set `kept_for_season` (or renew the membership) between candidate selection and release and assert no release; simulate with a seam or two interleaved transactions.

6. LOW-MEDIUM, cutoff release emails: the queue drains at cron step 0, before your step 1b3, so queued `lockerReleased` mail would wait a day while the member's 7 days are already running. Fix: after step 1b3, if anything was enqueued by it, drain the queue again in the same cron run (reuse `drainEmailQueue`), respecting the existing daily send budget; and compute `cleanout_due_at` for cutoff releases as 7 days from the cron run (unchanged) but make the email state the actual date ("by {date}") rather than "within 7 days", so a delayed send can never promise more time than the clean-out date gives. Apply the explicit-date wording to all three end types (revoked, released, not_renewed) and to the attest page notice if it is cheap there; otherwise leave the page as "within 7 days" and say so.

7. LOW, move (`lockers.ts`): the new allocation must copy `allocated_at` from the ended one (spec 13J: move preserves state), otherwise a holder moved after the cutoff gains the "allocated after cutoff" exemption. The UI "since" then means holder since. Test it.

8. LOW, bulk create (`locker-inventory.ts`): use `onConflictDoNothing()` and compute `skipped` from the rows actually returned, so two concurrent bulk-adds cannot 500 on the unique index.

9. LOW-MEDIUM, policy file name: a non-ASCII name (e.g. an en dash from a Word export) in `Content-Disposition` can throw `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` when the header is written. Emit an ASCII fallback `filename="..."` (replace non-ASCII and quotes) plus `filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded>`; use the same safe name for the email attachment. Test with a name containing an en dash and one containing a double quote.

Not required: the possible cutoff-vs-move deadlock (note it in risks only). Do NOT add a release cap or a "run now" mechanism.

UI consequences for phase 2: the cutoff panel must show the `cannotEvaluate` list with both reasons in plain words ("Not linked to a member" / "No membership season recorded, check manually"); the settings card must explain that the cutoff cannot be set while Lockers is off (it is hidden then anyway) ; and member-facing release copy uses the explicit date.

In your final report add a section "Review fixes" listing each of the nine with the commit hash and the test that covers it.

## What

A Lockers module, replacing SMLSC's Google Form + Apps Script + spreadsheet locker system. It is off for every tenant until a global admin switches it on.

## Journey

1. **Global admin** switches on Lockers for a club on the platform Tenants page. Club admins cannot see or change this.
2. **Member** requests a locker through the existing request form: on its own (button on the club page, or the locker QR, both open `/request?type=locker`), or as an add-on to a new fob request so details are entered once.
3. **Approver** opens the new Lockers tab, sees pending requests with a suggested locker, and approves (which allocates in the same step) or declines with a reason.
4. **Locker manager** maintains areas and lockers, moves members, and works a to-do list of labels to update and lockers to clean out.
5. **Member** sees their locker on their dashboard; admins see it on the member page next to credentials.
6. **Season confirmation** asks a locker holder whether they want to keep it. No releases it.
7. **Renewal cutoff**: a club-set date (month and day). After it, lockers held by members not renewed for the season are released and sent to the locker managers to clean out.

## Permissions

Two new permissions, separate from all existing ones:

| Permission | Can |
| --- | --- |
| Approve lockers | approve, decline, revoke, assign directly |
| Update lockers | areas and inventory, move, label and clean-out tasks; receives clean-out notices |

Club admins and global admins hold both, as with every permission.

## Safety properties

- `lockersEnabled` can only be changed by `PATCH /api/v1/platform/tenants/[id]` (global admin). The club settings route strips it, whatever the body.
- Every lockers route returns 404 while the module is off.
- Every state change starts with a guarded write, so two admins cannot both approve one request or allocate one locker.
- A released locker is not suggested or allocated during the member's clean-out window unless the admin explicitly overrides.
- The cutoff is armed when it is saved: a cutoff saved (or a module switched on) after this season's date first applies next season. - A signed-out request is never bound to a member account; the approver sees it flagged.
- Emails are sent for allocation, decline, revoke and release, with the club's locker policy attached where one is uploaded. All user-supplied text is escaped.

## Data

Migration `0021_lockers.sql`: four new tenant-scoped tables (RLS enabled and forced) and one nullable column on `attestation_requests`. Purely additive.

`packages/db/src/import-lockers.ts` imports the legacy spreadsheet: dry run by default, `--commit` refuses a tenant that already has lockers, never sends email. It has only been run as a dry run against a local test database. No spreadsheet data is in this repository.

## Verification

- Local, uncached, embedded Postgres: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, 619 tests passing (shared 34, db 35, web 550), 0 skipped; drift check and `bun run build` pass.

2. CROSS-SUITE INTERFERENCE (a flaky failure waiting to happen on main).
